record.paper_title: Recent results on functional equations in a single variable, perspectives and open problems
record.context_brief: Dimension bound for extended replicativity solutions
record.original_question: Let λ assign coefficients defining the extended replicativity system discussed in the paper, and consider its solution space inside L^1(R/Z). Is the complex-linear space of all L^1(R/Z) solutions always at most two-dimensional?

evidence.quote: The following question was posed by L. G. Lucht [169] in connection with the above system. Assume λ : N → CN. Is it true that the C-linear space of all its solutions ϕ ∈ L1(R/Z) is at most two-dimensional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{T}=\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$ and consider $L^1(\mathbb{T})$, the complex Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable $1$-periodic complex-valued functions on $\mathbb{R}$. For each positive integer $n$, define the dilation operator $D_n: L^1(\mathbb{T})\to L^1(\mathbb{T})$ by
$$(D_n\varphi)(x) \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\varphi\!\left(\frac{x+k}{n}\right)\quad (x\in\mathbb{T}).$$
Fix a function $\lambda:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{C}^{\mathbb{N}}$, written $\lambda(n)=(\lambda_n(m))_{m\in\mathbb{N}}$, providing coefficients for an extended replicativity system. Consider the linear functional equation, in the unknown $\varphi\in L^1(\mathbb{T})$,
$$D_n\varphi \;=\; \sum_{m\in\mathbb{N}}\lambda_n(m)\,\varphi(m\,\cdot)\qquad\text{for every }n\in\mathbb{N},$$
(where the right-hand side is assumed to converge in $L^1(\mathbb{T})$). Let $V_\lambda\subseteq L^1(\mathbb{T})$ denote the $\mathbb{C}$-linear space of all solutions $\varphi$ of this system.

Question: Is it true that, for every admissible choice of $\lambda$, the dimension of $V_\lambda$ over $\mathbb{C}$ is at most $2$?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return conclusive evidence that the question of whether the complex linear space of $L^1(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})$ solutions of the extended replicativity system (as posed by L. G. Lucht) is at most two-dimensional has been resolved. No publication explicitly settling the conjecture was located, so the status is recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Replicativity and Function Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Reference to Lucht's work on replicativity in function spaces, but no resolution of the dimensional bound question was found.
status_evidence.claim: Background reference connecting replicativity to function spaces; does not resolve the two-dimensionality question.
